newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian shares end higher, regain Monday's.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian shares end higher, regain Monday's.

text.p: Hungarian share prices rebounded on Tuesday more than making up for Monday's losses, traders said.
The BUX index finished at 5,506.52 points, up 63.94.
Analysts said the Dow's movements were important from the Hungarian market's point of view but other factors also had their effect.
"If the Dow Jones moves strongly one way or the other the Hungarian market usually ends up following it in the short-term," said Tommy Erdei of ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
"But for the time being we're going to see the market driven by a couple of bigger money managers out there, deciding on what companies they want to hold in their portfolios and what they don't."
Traders said investors were hungry for any news.

"The market starts to be increasingly nervous with investors beginning to lose their patience," said Szabolcs Gyongyosi of Daewoo Securities, adding demand in MOL shares has been on the rise as the company is preparing for a new phase of its selloff.
"Before the MOL issue they began to buy good volumes in MOL."
MOL shares strengthened to a daily high of 3,100 forints before retreating to end at 3,060, up 35.
The market's newcomer, curtain factory Gardenia, continued its rally up to a daily high of 1,990 forints in heavy trade before retreating to close at 1,980, up 215.
BUX futures closed higher for all maturities. June BUX finished at 5,839.5 points, up 75.
The market's short-term outlook was seen remaining flat after massive gains earlier this year, analysts said.
"After the first couple of months of strong fund flows to the market we saw people start to consolidate their holdings, reviewing what they had bought," Erdei said.
"I think we can more or less expect the same trend to continue for the next month or so, until earnings come out."
